<!-- pr-reviewer: 67451c1817f1ebb2e38ad8c656947c5f4ca2f4e6 -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

**What looks good**
- One legal room: `in_band` (crates/pathkernel/src/link/proof.rs:122) reads the entry stage's `legal_room` (`entry::legal_room`, now `pub(crate)`), so the link stage and the entry stage prove the same room. No second definition. `region_build.rs:123` reduces the air by the part zone, and the entry stage keeps its own smaller air only beside such a part.
- The air leaves out the part zone (crates/pathkernel/src/region_build.rs:123), so a link cannot cross a part that reaches out of the stock. The air walk of the edge route (crates/pathkernel/src/link/route.rs:76) is proved by the same chord test, so the bite of the air cannot be walked across.
- The region keeps the part zone (`with_part_zone`, crates/pathkernel/src/region.rs:161, crate-private). It is empty for `Inside` regions and for regions built by `PlanarRegion::new` directly; the proof then refuses the band there, as before.
- The zone stays consistent with the K4 counts: the swath test is unchanged, the K4 pins and the lift counts are cited in the decision doc (`docs/decisions/4241-kernel-link-edge-band.md`) and the law suite confirms them.

**Results (locally, worktree cc-pr4253-review, against origin/side/path-kernel 7f70d8b1a7fa9b6ae767eb1c63f3fb299548d055)**
- Trial merge: clean. `git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/side/path-kernel` prints "Already up to date" (the PR is entirely on top of its base; the merge-base is the base head). `gh pr view` says `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`.
- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel`: pass.
- `camcraft-pathkernel` `laws` suite: 129 passed, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-motion` `kernel_laws` suite: 29 passed, 0 failed.
- The four edge-band pins, by name, all passed:
  - `a_link_in_the_edge_band_over_uncut_stock_is_refused` (`UNCUT_STOCK`)
  - `a_link_in_the_edge_band_near_a_keep_out_is_refused` (`HITS_FIXTURE`)
  - `a_link_beside_a_part_that_reaches_out_of_the_stock_is_refused` (`CUTS_PART`; no stay link across the part in the air)
  - `a_link_leaves_a_cut_at_the_stock_edge_runs_in_the_air_and_comes_back_over_cleared_stock` (`UNCUT_STOCK` with no cut at the start; stays through the air with one)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass (no warnings).
- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-motion`: pass (via the kernel_laws build).

**Targeted tests**: the touched suites are `camcraft-pathkernel` `laws` and `camcraft-motion` `kernel_laws`; both ran and pass. No post or old toolpath changed, so no `example_catalog*` runs. No heavy lanes: the PR is a kernel sub-PR with no planner calling it, labelled P7, and the PR body records the same. The light lane is not exercised for the same reason — the light lane covers motion/app light twins, neither of which reaches this diff, and the touched suites pass in debug. The full heavy lanes are not run by design (they run at the cut, in the cut gate).

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The PR carries two priority labels (P2 and P7). The issue #4241 is P7. Per the issue law, an issue with two priority labels is reported to the maintainer; read it by the lower number until he decides.
2. The law check's `off_band` (crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/link_rule.rs:87) measures a point deep inside the part zone beside a part that reaches out of the stock as in the band: the `wall` term is 0 when the point is farther than the radius from the zone loop, so the check can pass a link that the kernel refuses. The dedicated pins cover the reach-out-of-stock case directly, and no fixture of the law suite has such a part, so this is not a false pass in practice — but the check's band definition is looser than the kernel's `in_band` for that shape. A one-line comment in the check would make that explicit.
3. The entry stage now reads the reduced air: its legal room gets smaller only beside a part that reaches out of the stock. This is disclosed in the PR body; no entry pin has such a part, so it is not exercised. Worth a future pin when the entry stage meets one.
4. The two band definitions (the kernel's `in_band`, from the legal room, and the law check's `off_band`, from the stock of the case) are deliberately separate, and the check comment says so. Keep them apart deliberately; do not unify them by reading the kernel's room here, or the law check can pass by copying the kernel's own definition.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
